Where the forecast ends, and local knowledge begins   +

Real data, transparent limits. Open-Meteo supplies hourly offshore total significant wave height, main swell height, mean swell period and direction, plus 10 m wind forecasts. NOAA CO-OPS supplies hourly astronomical tide predictions in feet above MLLW after unit conversion. Pacific time follows daylight saving automatically. Retrieval time is not model initialization time.

These are not breaking-wave forecasts. Offshore Hs averages the highest third of modeled waves. Shoaling, refraction, island shadowing and sandbars affect the surf at each beach. We show the selected marine grid coordinates and do not invent face heights. Wind orientation uses an approximate shore normal (La Jolla 270°, Huntington 225°, Malibu 180°); it is not a high-resolution exposure model.

Recommendation rules are conservative, unvalidated screening heuristics. Beginners are considered only at La Jolla Shores, with an instructor and an on-site check. Offshore Hs limits are 0.8 / 1.8 / 2.8 m for beginner / intermediate / advanced; beginner wind above 10 kn or mean swell period at least 13 s excludes the window. Period at least 14 s prompts caution. Winds at least 20 kn exclude all profiles. Predicted tide below 0.6 m MLLW at the reference station excludes the rocky Malibu option. These values are not universal safety thresholds or measured rock clearance.

Missing required data or data retrieved over 30 minutes ago prevents a recommendation. A failed feed stays unavailable; it is never replaced with demo conditions. The app caches complete responses for 15 minutes in this browser tab. Best option means the highest screening category at the selected hour, with geographic list order breaking ties, not a prediction of the best surf of the day.

Physics: deep-water energy density scales with Hs²; power per metre of wave crest approximately with Hs² × energy period. The displayed mean swell period is not energy period, so this app does not derive a power or safety score from it. Board advice also depends on actual face shape, rider ability, volume and rocker.

Data credits: Open-Meteo Marine and Weather API, using their Best Match models from providers including ECMWF, NOAA NCEP, DWD and Météo-France / Copernicus Marine. Model attribution and licenses. Tides: NOAA CO-OPS. Free Open-Meteo access is for noncommercial use; a commercial product needs an appropriate subscription.

Spot descriptions link to official beach authorities. The regional tide stations are La Jolla (9410230), Los Angeles (9410660) and Santa Monica (9410840). Tide predictions exclude storm surge and do not represent exact beach water levels. Water quality, closures, active marine warnings and crowds require the linked local checks. A forecast never replaces a lifeguard or local instructor’s assessment.
